summary:
Ice Hunter is a free web tool that lets anyone watch a patch of sky change over time in SPHEREx data. You enter an RA/Dec, or pick a built-in target such as WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, ε Indi B, RW Aurigae or R Draconis. The app pulls small SPHEREx cutouts from NASA/IPAC IRSA, aligns each observation epoch onto one sky grid and plays them like a short film. Difference images, Gaia and AllWISE overlays, proper-motion tracks and quality-flag masks help separate movers and variable stars from fixed sources. Clicking a source gives a spectrum across SPHEREx’s 102 bands. These spectra feed an Ice Lab that measures H₂O, CO₂ and CO ice features.

It answers the challenge by making a hard archive workflow, normally scripts and FITS files, a single link with no install. That matters because it opens SPHEREx to students, citizen scientists and researchers doing quick looks, and views can be shared or embedded by URL.
details:
Ice Hunter is a single-page web app for exploring SPHEREx sky images over time. The user enters an RA/Dec or picks a built-in target (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, ε Indi B, RW Aurigae, R Draconis). The app searches IRSA’s TAP service for every SPHEREx observation covering that patch and downloads small cutouts. Our own code reads the FITS files and uses each image’s sky coordinates (WCS) to align all observations onto one north-up grid. It masks flagged pixels, removes the smooth background, and combines images into epochs.

The epochs play like a short video. Difference modes subtract the first, previous or median epoch to highlight change. Gaia and AllWISE overlays and proper-motion tracks separate known stars from movers. Clicking a source gives a spectrum across the 102 bands, which can be sent to an Ice Lab that measures H₂O, CO₂ and CO ice features. Any view can be shared as a URL, and the app opens with a 10-second animated intro.

Benefits

  • It needs no install, accounts or coding.
  • It runs on a laptop or a phone browser, and hosting is free.
  • It brings time-lapse, spectra and ice analysis into one place.
  • Because it queries IRSA directly, new data releases show up without rebuilding the app.

Intended impact
We want SPHEREx data to be usable by students, teachers, citizen scientists and outreach groups, not only researchers. It also gives researchers a quick first look at movers, variable stars and ice-bearing clouds before heavier analysis.

Tools, languages and software

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Canvas, in one self-contained file
  • A custom FITS reader and TAN WCS reprojection
  • NASA/IPAC IRSA TAP and the cutout service
  • Gaia DR3 and AllWISE via CDS VizieR
  • Chromium with Playwright for testing
  • Python (Pillow) for artwork and PptxGenJS for slides
  • GitHub Pages for hosting
  • SI (AI) tools, Claude, helped with code, text and artwork. This should be disclosed in your submission.

No special hardware was used.

Creativity

  • The Ice Lab links a time-lapse tool to spectral analysis, using the 102 bands rather than just single images.
  • The solar-system intro turns into the “ICE HUNT” title.
  • A simulated-data mode keeps the tool usable when the archive can’t be reached.

Factors we considered

  • Anyone should be able to use it, with simple controls and a share link.
  • Browsers can’t always call IRSA directly, so we included an optional proxy and a demo fallback.
  • Cutouts include a large PSF cube, so downloads are budgeted by number of images.
  • Quality flags are shown and maskable.
  • Some preset coordinates and proper motions are approximate and should be checked.
